fixed_myself.what: A percentage rounded a short figure up to the one it missed. Of the 99 pace ratios the payload carries, 38 sit between 0.995 and 1 and every one printed 100%, beside the 7 that are exactly 1 and printed the same string. A campaign short of its reference and a campaign level with it were one number on the screen, and the percentage is the number a reader on this row takes at face value.
fixed_myself.how: Whole percent is kept everywhere, except that a value below 100 which would round to 100 is floored to one decimal, so the residual rounding only ever goes down and a figure that is short says so. Proven against HEAD's own module in node: HEAD answers 100% for 0.9989 and 0.9996, the fix answers 99.8% and 99.9%, and 1 still answers 100%, 1.04 still 104%, 0.88 still 88%. Measured on the shipped Hebrew board: occurrences of 100% fell from 46 to 7, and 99.6%, 99.7%, 99.8% and 99.9% appeared where a hundred used to be. CMP_D040's money line now reads 99.8% בקצב.

fixed_myself.what: The ledger's own sign-off sentence says this product records who acted, and the trail printed the actor only when the store had one. On a server with an uninitialised account store, which is how this product runs before an operator creates the first account, every record was written with raised_by empty and the trail said when and quietly dropped who. Tri-state was broken: the unknown was omitted rather than stated.
fixed_myself.how: One actorClause(who, locale) used by both sites, which names the actor when there is one and otherwise says so. Driven in a browser: the trail reads נרשמה 08/08/2026, 18:46 UTC על ידי חשבון שהמוצר לא רשם. נספר נכון ל-27/04/2025, 22:59, and the closure line reads the same clause under its reason.

fixed_myself.what: The drill's dropped-spots sentence disagreed with its own number in its commonest case. Of the 32 sourced day rows in data/campaign_delivery.csv that carry a dropped count, 21 carry exactly 1, so the sentence a reader met most often was 1 מתוכם הושמטו, a plural verb on a single spot, and 1 of them left out by a booking rule, which is not a sentence. The Hebrew numeral was also unisolated at the head of a right-to-left run.
fixed_myself.how: droppedSentence(count, locale) picks the clause by the count and isolates the numeral in the plural branch. Measured in the drill: אחד מתוכם הושמט בגלל כלל הזמנה.

fixed_myself.what: The row the keyboard is on was a colour and nothing else. After the place marker returned a reader to row 13 of 56, the marked row carried aria-current null, id null and tabindex null, and the list carries role=list with no aria-activedescendant, so the only signal that j and k had moved was the 2 px ring the sheet draws.
fixed_myself.how: aria-current on the focused listitem, which is valid there and moves no focus, so the list keeps the key handler it owns. Measured in a browser: exactly one element carries aria-current=true and it moves with j. The remaining half, a roving tabindex that announces the move as it happens, is left in the queue because it changes which element the keydown starts from and I will not ship an unmeasured focus change.

blind_ab: Google Ads for pacing against a flight, Stripe for how a shortfall states its remedy, both opened and read this round. Where this board wins: it publishes its trigger. The pace verdict is decided at 0.95 and 0.85, both on the payload with the sentence that they are the product's rule and not a commercial term, while Google's optimization score is described as calculated in real-time from statistics, settings and recent recommendation history and the formula is never given. It also refuses where the references would guess: a flight with one elapsed day unsourced returns unknown with gap_in_elapsed and lists the missing dates, where a budget board would divide by the days it has. And every figure prints the scope it was counted over on the same line, which neither reference does. Where Stripe wins: its invoice status table publishes, for every state, what you may do from it, so the machine is legible before you own a record in it. This ledger shows the acts only on the record in front of you, and its two kind chips hide their meaning in a title attribute. Where Google Ads wins, and it is the sharper loss: a recommendation is applied on the row with its impact quantified, while the primary remedy on 51 of the 56 rows here is a link to another screen to upload a file. That is honest, because the delivery feed does not exist, but the do-the-recommended-thing leg of JS-6 completes on this board only through the acceptance. Where they draw: both offer a reversal that keeps a record rather than deleting one, Google through change history and this through the published withdrawal, and this one is better published because the reason and the state come off the store on the answer to the write instead of being a constant the client holds.
